TOP: Xen Orchestra auth bypass exploited to hijack VM servers
Nitori, Grok Build and Railway leaks expose millions of records
Microsoft: under 10 neurons can backdoor an AI agent
Claude Meetings brings AI into video calls

P.h: Critical Xen Orchestra auth bypass is exploited to hijack VM servers
P.p: TLDR InfoSec reports a critical authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra, the web platform for managing XCP-NG virtualization hosts. A remote attacker with network access to the management portal can send a specially crafted cookie to retrieve login tokens, run arbitrary code on managed pools and fully compromise the cluster.
P.s: The flaw is under active exploitation. Upgrade now and take the management portal off the public internet.

items.h: Nitori says hackers stole 37.6M customer records
items.d: The Japanese furniture giant exposed member, customer and corporate data: names, emails, addresses, phones, birth dates and order details. It says no passwords or card numbers were taken.

items.h: Grok Build agent leaks confidential apps, some from SpaceXSI
items.d: Claroc found more than 35,000 public Grok Build apps via passive DNS enumeration, because URL randomness sat in the subdomain. Exposed: sales plans, 3,784 medical exams, Tesla scorecards.

items.h: Railway breach led to $740K in fraudulent AI charges
items.d: An October intrusion exposed up to 100,000 customers' workspace environment variables. The attacker wanted AI provider credentials. Rotate keys stored in Railway env vars.

items.h: Fireworks AI: second intrusion reached datasets and partial weights
items.d: Fireworks expanded its October disclosure on November 9. Hackers reached customer datasets, partial model weights and billing data.

P.h: Microsoft shows AI agents can be backdoored by editing under 10 neurons
P.p: Both TLDR InfoSec and TLDR IT cover Microsoft's Lazarus research. Editing fewer than 10 rarely used neurons in an open-weight model embeds a hidden command. When a trigger shows up in a prompt or tool output, the agent may run attacker commands with its existing permissions. Testing hit 98.8% on Nemotron-Terminal-8B using seven edited neurons.
P.s: Microsoft advises comparing checkpoints with base weights, using private model registries, sandboxing agent code, limiting network access and requiring approval for high-impact actions.

items.h: Artex AI pen-test tool repurposed by attackers
items.d: Storm-0940 used the open-source framework for more than 151,000 auth requests against eight organizations, then stole ConnectWise OAuth credentials and hit over 2,250 downstream Microsoft 365 and Azure environments.

items.h: Codex prompt injection put npm releases at risk
items.d: Depi researchers chained a GitHub issue injection into shell commands, runner credential theft and build cache poisoning, one maintainer action from a backdoored @openai/codex. OpenAI fixed it first.

items.h: Falcon C2 planted in 39 Roundcube portals
items.d: A script tag in page headers loaded a browser-only C2 that steals passwords, emails and cookies. Unit 42 links it to PeckBirdy. Audit webmail templates for unknown script tags.

items.h: M365 session revocation still leaves a 90-minute window
items.d: A revoked access token can live up to 90 minutes. Critical event evaluation does not cut Graph API access, so only disabling the account cuts it off at once.

P.h: Claude joins video calls with Meetings, Whiteboards and Sheets
P.p: TLDR IT says Anthropic announced Claude Meetings, which joins Google Meet calls, takes notes, retrieves information and drafts action plans while people are still talking. It is in beta for Team and Enterprise customers and puts Anthropic in closer competition with Microsoft and Google.
P.s: New interactive connectors let users work inside Adobe, Notion, Atlassian, Salesforce and HubSpot from within Claude. Review what meeting data connectors can reach.

tiles.t: Yandex restores 97% of data after drone strikes
tiles.d: 2.84% is lost for good because customers had no backups. Backups will be on by default.
CNCF: turn unwritten guardrails into machine-readable policy, scoped identities and control loops.

tiles.t: IBM and Microsoft launch Imagine Enterprise
tiles.d: 6,000 prebuilt agents on Azure, Entra, Purview, Defender. Customers still own compliance.

tiles.t: Data center power demand outruns the grid
tiles.d: Demand up about 19% a year versus 2% grid growth, per Howden. Up to 58% may need off-grid power by 2030.

tiles.t: Adobe opens Creative Cloud to AI via MCP

items.h: Nvidia works with outside firm to find CEO candidates
items.d: TLDR says Nvidia is exploring a successor to Jensen Huang after reports of extramarital affairs. The board is weighing an interim chief.

items.h: AWS Emulator gives coding agents a local AWS
items.d: Agents can build and test most software against it, leaving engineers to decide what gets built and whether it is right. Code is public.

items.h: Gemini Decisions API scores up to 1,000 questions in one pass
items.d: Takes text, images, audio, video and PDF. Priced at $0.10 per 2M tokens, outputs free, in Google AI Studio.
Each delegation method fails differently. Forking beats summarization but costs more as context grows; a selective fork is proposed.

tiles.t: Anthropic adds up to $4.3B in Microsoft compute deals
tiles.d: Capacity ahead of its planned IPO.
Control Room halts research model output within 35 seconds. It wants to cut that delay.
Experts verified the Yang-Mills result but do not yet fully understand it.
